items.title: No local estimate of the cut-off's accuracy
items.whyItMatters: The only accuracy estimate comes from two other hospitals and chose its threshold in its own data (claim c1).
items.opportunity: Measure sensitivity and specificity at 30 or below in the next four intakes with the threshold fixed in advance.

items.title: Predictive values depend on the local separation rate
items.whyItMatters: At 12 to 27 percent separation the positive predictive value moved from 0.21 to 0.44 (claim c3), which decides how many flagged residents would stay anyway.
items.opportunity: Report predictive values at the observed rate and at the hospital's recent range of 19 to 26 percent.

items.title: Internal transfers could be counted as separations
items.whyItMatters: Reason codes misclassify transfers as resignations (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Define the target condition as leaving the hospital by date; count transfers between units as staying.

items.title: Residents who leave before month 3 are never screened
items.whyItMatters: Early leavers are outside the index test's reach and would be invisible in the accuracy estimate.
items.opportunity: Count them in the flow diagram and report them separately.

items.title: Accuracy may differ by rotation pattern and campus
items.whyItMatters: Residents on night-heavy rotations or at the rural campus may score and leave for different reasons, so one cut-off could fail them.
items.opportunity: Report accuracy descriptively by rotation pattern and campus without choosing subgroup thresholds.

errorsFound: The need assumes a low score means a resident will leave; in the retrieved accuracy study about two flagged residents stayed for every one who left.
reevaluation: The gaps point to a small, pre-specified local accuracy study with a fixed cut-off, a date-based reference standard and predictive values at the local rate before any booster depends on the score.
summary: Five gaps: no local accuracy, prevalence-dependent predictive values, transfer misclassification, unscreened early leavers, and possible subgroup differences.
